reauth_confirm.description: Paperless no longer accepts the API token. Enter a new token of the same Paperless user.

data_description.api_token: API token of the Paperless user that Home Assistant uses

reconfigure.title: Change the Paperless connection
reconfigure.description: The token must belong to the same Paperless user as before. Enter the token again.

data_description.url: Address of your Paperless-ngx server, for example http://192.168.1.10:8000
data_description.api_token: API token of the Paperless user that Home Assistant uses
data_description.verify_ssl: Check the TLS certificate of the server (recommended)

insecure_http.title: Unencrypted connection
insecure_http.description:
The address starts with http://, so the API token and your documents travel unencrypted over the network. This is only acceptable on a trusted local network. Use https:// when Paperless is reachable through a reverse proxy.

Submit to continue anyway.

permissions_warning.title: Paperless user can do more than read
permissions_warning.description:
The Paperless user {username} is a superuser or may add, change or delete data. Home Assistant only reads from Paperless, so a dedicated user with view permissions only is safer.

Submit to continue anyway.

error.missing_permission: The Paperless user lacks these permissions: {permissions}.

init.title: Paperless Lookup options
init.description: Choose what to change. After each step you return to this menu. Changes are only stored with Save and close; closing with X discards them.

access.title: Access tag and visibility
access.description: Only Paperless documents with this tag are visible in Home Assistant.

data.panel_users: Users who see Paperless Lookup in the sidebar

data_description.access_tag: Without an access tag, no document is visible.
data_description.admins_always: Home Assistant administrators get access to every category.
data_description.panel_users: None chosen: everyone sees it. This only concerns the menu item; which documents someone may see is chosen per category.

categories.title: Categories
categories.description: A category is a Paperless document type. Documents of other types, or without a type, are not visible. Next, choose the users per category.

data_description.categories: Only documents of the chosen document types can be shown in Home Assistant.

category_users.title: Users per category
category_users.description: Choose, per category, the Home Assistant users that may see its documents. Administrators see every category while Administrators see all categories is on. Who sees the sidebar item is set separately under Access tag and visibility.

devices.title: Devices
devices.description: Documents of a device category (for example manuals) are linked to devices through a custom field with one or more models, separated by ;.

data_description.device_categories: Only categories chosen under Categories are listed.
data_description.model_field: Paperless custom field (text) with the device models.
data_description.zigbee2mqtt_fallback: Link to the Zigbee2MQTT device page when a Zigbee device has no manual.

follow_reads.title: Follow who opens documents
follow_reads.description:
Per user, choose the categories to follow. Every time that user opens or downloads a document of such a category, the Home Assistant logbook gets an entry with the user, the time, the document number and the category (never the title). Thumbnails are not counted, and the same file opened again within a minute counts once. Each user only gets the categories they may see.

Not listed, because they may not see any category: {without_access}.

To see only these entries, filter the logbook on the device Paperless Lookup.

update_failed.message: Failed to read the documents from Paperless.

unsupported_version.title: Paperless-ngx version not supported
unsupported_version.description: Paperless Lookup needs Paperless-ngx 3.0 or newer, so the integration could not start. Update Paperless-ngx, then reload the integration.

missing_permission.title: Paperless user lacks permissions
missing_permission.description: The Paperless user that Home Assistant uses lacks these permissions: {permissions}. The integration could not start. Give the user these view permissions in Paperless under Users & Groups, then reload the integration.

access_tag_missing.title: Paperless access tag not available
access_tag_missing.description: No documents are visible in Home Assistant: no access tag is chosen, or the Paperless user cannot see it. In Paperless, create the tag or share it with that user. Or choose another one under Settings > Devices & services > Paperless Lookup > Configure > Access tag and visibility. This message disappears at the next refresh, or when you reload the integration.
